programs.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programs.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programs.title: Living Arts of Huizhou
programs.desc: This is Huangshan in eastern China. In this city, you’ll encounter one of China’s most traditional building styles: Hui-style architecture. How does Hui style set this region apart? What’s life like for people living in these houses? With these questions in mind, we’re embarking on a journey to decode Hui-style architecture.

programs.title: China Bound: Chongqing
programs.desc: Join us in southwest China's Chongqing, one of the world's biggest cities. From futuristic skylines and cyberpunk streets, to fire-breathing opera, spicy hotpot and kungfu tea, we're diving deep into this megacity the size of Austria.

programs.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.1: Old Gems
programs.desc: Xiamen, a key starting point of China’s ancient Maritime Silk Road, is one of China’s most livable cities. In this episode, host Min-Zhui Lee and co-host Pan William, an honorary citizen of Xiamen and a professor, take you on an immersive journey through the city. Explore Xiamen University, renowned as China’s most beautiful university campus, and visit Wanshi Park, known as “China’s First Lawn”. Trace Xiamen’s history through its streets, admiring the arcades that tell the stories of the city’s early commercial development. Finally, board a boat to Gulangyu Islet, the “Island of Music” — the birthplace of modern music education in China, and a living “World Architecture Museum”. Every corner of this islet lets you experience the past and present of Xiamen’s vibrant life.

programs.title: Crunch and Munch in Macao Ep.4
programs.desc: Feast on the stories behind Macao's iconic dishes and its people - One Country, Two Systems, endless flavors.

programs.title: Art Folk
programs.desc: Art Folk is a colorful celebration of the lives of four remarkable rural residents, each with a particular artistic talent, featuring film, poetry, visual arts and musical instrument-making. Debuting on February 28, it recounts stories about how China's countryside serves as the backdrop to–and even the inspiration for–the local farmers in their pursuit of a richer and more varied cultural life.

programs.title: Aerial China III Ep.5
programs.desc: Tianjin is a city whose waterways all converge in one place: the Haihe River. Indeed, you could say that, in a sense, this river is a living, flowing chronicler of China's metamorphosis - the golden thread that traces a century of history from the Grand Canal to the open vistas of the country's ocean-going future.

programs.title: Yuxian, a living legacy of ancient architecture and paper-cutting
The Taste of Yunnan Ep.1
programs.desc: This ten-part documentary introduces the food of Yunnan, from the opening chapters "Family Feast in Spring" and "Simple Joys" to the nostalgic "Times Past" and "Love Away from Home." While each chapter seems to stand alone, they share a common core. Unlike conventional food documentaries, The Taste of Yunnan leaps across the region and avoids categorizing by locality or dish. Instead, every episode follows its own protagonists: the Zheng Hongwei brothers harvesting water bamboo shoots in Jianshui; Yang Jimei's family gathering toon sprouts at the foot of Jizu Mountain in Binchuan, Dali; and Wang Jinghua, a young man of the Nu ethnic group who still makes the traditional Nujiang dish "chicken cooked in lacquer tree oil" entirely by hand. Through its plain yet detailed portrayal of food and its subtle understanding of the relationship between people and ingredients, the series is much more than a food documentary. It challenges the old misperception that Yunnan cuisine lacks cultural depth, showing that its heritage is humble and simple - found in a piece of Heqing's secret-recipe blown liver from Dali, or in a jar of Yinji pickles from Weishan.

programs.title: Fujian's Tulou - The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programs.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programs.title: China Bound: Guangzhou
programs.desc: Join us in Guangzhou, a global manufacturing hub in south China with a population as large as New York's. From browsing hip street markets to wholesale clothes shopping, sampling world-famous Cantonese cuisine, and visiting the childhood home of kungfu legend Bruce Lee, there is plenty to do during our stay.

programs.title: Enchanting Xiamen Ep.2: New Jewel
programs.desc: In the second episode of our Xiamen series, host Tianran He and co-host Laura, an American who has lived in Xiamen for 7 years, guide you to discover Xiamen's internationalization, modernization, and unique fashion vibe. First, they cycle along the island road, taking in the stunning coastal scenery of the famous Round-the-Island Road, and step into Zengcuoan — once a small fishing village, now a thriving creative hub — to showcase its remarkable transformation. Next, Laura leads Tianran to experience the daily life of expats in Xiamen: exploring the lively coffee bar street, and joining a fun gathering at a stylish French restaurant. A passionate lover of Chinese culture, Laura invites Tianran to experience a traditional Chinese tea ceremony. After that, the pair head to Xiamen’s fashion central business district, experimenting with bold new looks in clothing stores that have caught the eye of the global fashion community. Finally, Tianran visits an egret habitat to meet photographers who document these beautiful birds, and together they admire the grace of Xiamen's iconic egrets.

programs.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.1
programs.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programs.title: Xizang Rhapsody
programs.desc: Xizang Rhapsody spotlights motivated young people across different fields in Xizang who follow their passion and defy preconceived notions about life there. Among them are Tashi Tsering, who pioneered Tibetan-language versions of globally popular children’s books; "Wootsang Dance Crew," the first street dance crew in Xizang; Tsomo, the region's first certified international coffee taster and founder of a "highland coffee lab;" electronic music lover Thubten Tenzin Chosphel; modern dancer Sonam Droma; and some of the first skateboarders in Lhasa. Told through their individual stories and viewpoints, the film reveals how tradition and modernity interact, and reflects Xizang's social progress and growing cultural diversity.

programs.title: Fearless Journey Ep.2
programs.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programs.title: Aerial China III Ep.6
programs.desc: Shanxi in north China is almost entirely covered with mountains. But the principal force that has sculpted this striking landscape out of the Taihang Mountains is the river that more than any other has shaped Chinese civilization - the Yellow River.

programs.title: Born to climb
programs.desc: Bobby, aka Lin Ziguan, is a passionate young climber in Wenzhou City, east China's Zhejiang Province. He first came across the sport when his parents took him to an indoor climbing facility at a local shopping mall for fun, and it was a case of love at first sight. To further fuel his passion, Bobby's father refurnished a room at home and turned it into a private rock-climbing gym. While many students find themselves "climbing the walls" with frustration on weeknights and grumbling at their homework, Bobby spends most of his free time clambering around the surfaces of his bedroom as he aspires to become a celebrated outdoor rock climber one day.
